purpose: Pass-1 source curation only; no independent claim verdicts or encounter rubrics

evidence.scope: Ancestry-only self-paced integration path, explicitly identified by the current AI-200 course UID and containing the three used messaging/Functions modules.
Ancestry-only module for broker topology, message envelopes and reliable processing; substantive units supply technical evidence.
Ancestry-only module for event origins, schemas, routing, delivery policy and publishing; substantive units supply technical evidence.
Ancestry-only module for Python function apps, hosting, local deployment, bindings and connection identities.

Broker queues absorb bursts and decouple request intake from processing. Standard and Premium have different capacity models. Queue allocation is not exactly-once processing; reliability claims use the separate receive-mode unit.

Queues allocate work among competing receivers; topic subscriptions receive independent copies. Sessions group ordered work. Subscription SQL, correlation and Boolean filters have different predicate capabilities and valid use cases.

Application properties carry routing metadata; message IDs support configured duplicate detection and correlation IDs track a request. Claim-check separates large data from broker messages, TTL bounds validity, and batches must retry the overflowing message in a new batch.

PeekLock and receive-and-delete trade settlement reliability for overhead. Complete, abandon, defer and dead-letter serve distinct outcomes. Delivery limits, explicit DLQ resubmission and lock renewal are documented; renewal does not guarantee exactly-once effects.

Custom topics receive application events, system topics receive provider events, subscriptions define selection/destination, and handlers process deliveries. Candidates avoid namespace MQTT and unbounded latency assertions.

CloudEvents fields distinguish origin, operation, identity and subject. Type, subject and typed-data filters can be combined. Custom-topic input and subscription output schemas have asymmetric compatibility.

Traditional custom-topic webhook delivery uses acknowledgement, endpoint-specific error treatment, time and attempt limits, optional Blob dead-letter storage and all-or-none batches. Selected claims exclude the introductory overgeneralization that every unsuccessful status retries.

Applications create custom topics and publish CloudEvents with SDK or REST. Managed-identity publication requires EventGrid Data Sender; events describe checkpoints and reference detailed outputs. No GitHub SDK link is admitted.

Hosting and initialization affect cold-start latency; function execution timeout differs from the HTTP response limit. Async intake can hand work to Service Bus. Candidates avoid absolute Premium cold-start promises and blanket unbounded-execution assertions.

Core Tools hosts local triggers; function_app.py, host.json, requirements.txt and .funcignore have separate roles. Azurite supplies local host storage. Deployment/settings commands must preserve production configuration. The Python reference resolves the unit’s overbroad publish-with-settings wording.

Python v2 uses decorators, one trigger and optional input/output bindings. Service Bus triggers and output parameters integrate queued work with storage. Reusing explicit SDK clients avoids per-invocation initialization. Preview SDK-type extensions are not used.

Local settings are separate from hosted app configuration. Fetching remote settings and local machine encryption support development workflows. Questions do not make immediate refresh claims about centralized configuration or secret references.

Named Service Bus identity connections pair a fullyQualifiedNamespace prefix with Receiver or Sender roles. Function/host/admin keys have separate scopes and do not identify callers. Host storage remains a separate dependency.

Python v2 route_params reads route segments; blueprints must be registered with the main app. requirements.txt drives remote dependencies, .funcignore excludes deployment files, and changing Python version requires rebuilding and redeploying artifacts. Preview or new worker-version controls are excluded.

Exactly one trigger invokes a function; optional input/output directions differ by binding. The 4.x table distinguishes Blob/Cosmos standalone input support from Service Bus/Event Grid trigger and output support. Python ServiceBusReceivedMessage SDK-type trigger is Preview and is not used.

The explicit compatibility table permits CloudEvents-to-CloudEvents and both Event Grid input output formats, but not CloudEvents input to Event Grid output. Candidate claims do not use the article’s old Functions runtime samples.

Concrete subject boundaries, scalar predicate types, AND across filters, OR within values, and missing-key behavior support exact routing evaluations. Scalar data paths avoid the article’s inconsistent CloudEvents top-level key descriptions.

Publishing authorization requires events/send/action, provided by EventGrid Data Sender. A resource, resource-group or subscription assignment has different scope. Token acquisition alone is not authorization; disableLocalAuth API examples are excluded.

A function app is the deployment/runtime-management boundary, whereas projects and blueprints organize code. Publishing targets an existing app; host storage and SDK clients are separate connection responsibilities.
